short: Uniform Sparsest Cut: no constant factor

title.title: Uniform sparsest cut: hardness and SDP gaps
title.subtitle: Claim: approximating Uniform Sparsest Cut within any fixed constant factor is NP-hard

plain: Split a network in two while cutting as few links as possible: even a rough answer is hard to find

beats.text: Sparsest cut: split the graph where few edges cross per pair of vertices separated
Arora–Rao–Vazirani approximate it within $O(\sqrt{\log n})$; no constant-factor hardness was known
Claimed: no constant factor unless P = NP, and an SDP gap of nearly $\sqrt{\log n}$

steps: Turn a formula into a proof that can be spot-checked
Build a network out of the spot-check's scores
A satisfying answer gives a cheap cut
Any cheap cut can be decoded back into an answer

achievement.label: Unconditional hardness for Uniform Sparsest Cut (open)
achievement.context: Before: constant-factor hardness only under Small-Set Expansion; SDP gaps $\exp(\Omega(\sqrt{\log\log n}))$
achievement.note: Only the SDP gap is in Lean; the NP-hardness is paper only

verify.detail: In Lean: the integrality-gap sequence only. The NP-hardness paper is not formalized
verify.ourCheck: We did not build the Lean or referee the proof

voice.text: Split a network evenly while cutting few links. The best algorithm loses a root log factor.
Formulas become networks whose cheap cuts decode back into answers.
Claimed: no constant factor is possible.

sources.quote: constant-factor hardness only under Small-Set Expansion (Raghavendra-Steurer-Tulsiani)
later improved (per the paper) to exp(Omega(sqrt(log log n))) by Kane-Meka
For every fixed C>1, approximating Uniform Sparsest Cut (unit demand on every pair, nonnegative rational capacities) within factor C is NP-hard
partial formalization: UniformSparsestCut.lean covers only the integrality-gap sequence; the NP-hardness paper is not formalized
